articles.headline: From Our Philadelphia Correspondent: A Busybody in Philadelphia (with the A. M. E. / A. M. E. Zion union circular)
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: This being the first opportunity offered me to address your numerous readers, on account of a multiplicity of business crowding me since my appointment as one of your Correspondents, permit me to offer a passing thought under the above caption, which may be of interest. It is a remarkable fact, that one favored with the power of vision, can scarcely pass through our city without observing nearly all kinds of bodies. [The writer charges that a 'Mr. Busybody' printed and sold for his own profit the union circular which the Wesley Church convention had ordered its committee (Revs. S. Jones, H. Davis, J. Trusty, J. Woodlye and A. L. Stanford) to publish; he likens the offender to 'that white devil which I saw the Rev. Wm H. Jones exhibiting at a Panoramic exhibition', then prints the circular 'Bethel Zion: The Union of the Two African Methodist Episcopal Churches'.] Unsigned.

articles.headline: A Soldier's Letter (55th Mass. Vols., Folly Island)
articles.summary: 55th Mass. Vols., Folly Island, May 29th, 1864. Dear Editor: I have attempted several times to give you a faint idea of the condition of things generally in my immediate neighborhood, concerning military affairs, and once more must I encroach upon your proverbial forbearance and generosity. [Complains that the regiment, enlisted on Governor Andrew's promise of equal pay, has served a year without a cent; 'Mr. Weaver, will you please insert this in your paper? ... I live in your city'; also denounces 'the cowardly villains at home' who are 'trying to bring our families to destruction'.] Signed 'A Sergeant of the 55th Mass.'

articles.headline: Justice Restored (editorial on the Philadelphia passenger railways, with the New York Ellen Anderson case)
articles.summary: We clip the following from the New York Tribune, and it will be read with much interest by our people. It is just what we would like to see in Philadelphia. But when, oh! when will the hard-hearted Passenger Railway Companies of Philadelphia give the right to the colored people to ride in the cars? They may stubbornly refuse, but there is a just God, who will make them yield at a time when they will wish that they had done justice to the oppressed. [Reprints 'Right of Colored People to Ride in the Street Cars: Important Case', the complaint of Mrs. Ellen Anderson, widow of a sergeant of the 26th Colored Regiment, ejected from an Eighth Avenue car in New York, and the company's order of June 23, 1864 admitting colored people to all its cars.]

articles.headline: No Difference Between the Black and White American
articles.author: J. Anderson Raymond
articles.summary: There is no natural difference existing between the two races. If the white and the black men's conditions had been the same, no difference could have been found between the two races, so far as intellect is concerned. The black man has the same number of bones as the white man; the same number of blood vessels; the same sutures in the skull; the same divisions of brain, and the same physical organization. J. Anderson Raymond, Philadelphia, July 12th, 1864.

articles.headline: The Colored People of Philadelphia (editorial)
articles.summary: We are rejoiced to know that there is an upward tendency of our people, morally, mentally, and industrially. Over four years ago, when we were sent to this city to take the charge of our paper and book concern, we thought that a great portion of our people were more addicted to the most degraded habits than any class in the city. [Blames Irish, Dutch and American-run rum holes in the small streets and alleys; reports improvement in the past eighteen months, crediting enlistment bounties, bootblack earnings from soldiers' boots, church-going and Recorder reading; rebukes the Philadelphia Evening Telegraph's 'Here and There' editorial of July 13th.]

articles.headline: The Colored People and the City Railways (with Rev. Wm. Johnson Alston's letter to the Press)
articles.author: Wm. Johnson Alston
articles.summary: Editorial introduction: 'We clip the following from the Press of last Thursday, 21st inst. Its subject is a minister of the gospel, a man of the highest repute among clerical bodies; and there is, in fact, only one thing repulsive to him in the drivers and conductors of the street cars: he is a colored man.' Letter: To the Christian Public of Philadelphia: Within the past week my only living child having been at death's door, by our physician we were directed to take him over the Delaware river as often as convenient. On our return to the Philadelphia side, on one occasion, the child became completely prostrated. [A Lombard and South Street car was hailed; the conductor refused him entry 'being colored' and ordered the driver on, though the only persons on the car were the conductor and driver. He asks whether it is manly to exclude respectable colored citizens from the Lombard and South St. cars when they pay taxes on real estate on that line worth over $100,000, while young colored men enlist (his two brothers among them) and his congregation keeps an auxiliary of the Women's Sanitary Commission.] Wm. Johnson Alston, Rector of St. Thomas' Prot. Episc. Church, July 19, 1864.

articles.headline: Hope On, Hope Ever (Prof. Johnson's lecture at Central Presbyterian Church)
articles.summary: An appreciating audience, however small, always does more towards encouraging a lecturer than a thousand persons who congregate for mere idle speculation. So it proved on last Wednesday evening, at Prof. Johnson's lecture in Central Presbyterian Church; for, though the number of persons did not reach two hundred, yet we doubt whether the Prof. ever had an audience that drank more eagerly in the instruction. [The assembly joined in singing 'Old John Brown'.]

articles.headline: Camden Correspondence (Woodbury literary entertainment; Macedonia debt and quarterly meeting; death of Sergeant Stidam)

[Rev. T. G. Steward lectured on 'The Black American' in the church of which Rev. Barney has charge; B. F. Brown, of Camden, spoke; $30 to $40 raised for the A. M. E. church at Woodbury; the ladies were Miss Mary Manly, Mrs. M. Still, Miss L. Dickinson, Mrs. L. G. Tudas and Mrs. S. Craig. Macedonia, Camden, paid $61 on its debt on Sabbath, July 3. W. D. W. Schureman at night. Professor Green lectured in Camden; Prof. W. H. Johnson, 'now operating in Philadelphia', expected. Death of Sergeant Stidam, of the Fifth Regiment of M. V., killed near Charleston; his widow, Mrs. E. A. Stidam, is a resident of Camden.] Signed 'West Jersey'.

articles.headline: Working for the Union, Right, Wrongs No One (W. H. Jones's defense of his union circular)
articles.author: Wm. H. Jones
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I am of the opinion, that persons who publicly denounce the conduct or doings of others, should, at least, think several times before they speak once. I find in your last two papers, an effort being made to stir up, if possible, a feeling against Wm. H. Jones, for, as is charged, publishing in circular form, the conclusions at which the Union Convention arrived. [He says the convention's basis of union was printed in the Philadelphia Inquirer and other papers, that he bought the paper and struck off circulars as others resold the papers, and that he gave nearly as many away as he sold.] Wm. articles.headline: The Colored Men in this State Have Been Loyal to the Government (editorial)
articles.summary: When we remember the position that our colored fellow-citizens took, at the outbreak of the present rebellion, in regard to the Union of the Government, which was loyal, in every sense of the word, and the treatment which they have received, we are at a loss to know what encouragement they have had to continue their loyalty. [Recounts the rejection of Philadelphia volunteers in 1861; the colored company that went to Harrisburg during Lee's invasion and was sent home ('Our friends, Mr. Catto, Jr., and Mr. J. C. articles.headline: A Sad Bereavement: drowning of Richard Allen Turner, Chester
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I feel it to be my duty to inform yourself and the numerous readers of your excellent paper of the occurrence of a most heart-rending and lamentable catastrophe in Chester lately. On the 6th of July last a youth, residing in Chester, by the name of Richard Allen Turner, left his father's house in company with another lad, who prevailed on him to go with him to the creek for the purpose of taking a bath, and while there he was drowned. His body was recovered the next day by the Rev. William Murphy. He was a teacher in the Sabbath School, and was the only son of the Rev. William H. and Hester Turner. He was about twelve years and four months old.

articles.headline: The First Colored Annual Conference under the Methodist Episcopal Church
articles.summary: The local preachers of the Methodist Episcopal Church were, on last Friday, the 29th ultimo, organized into an Annual Conference by Rev. Bishop Janes, assisted by Bishop Simpson, Dr. Durbin, and others, in the John Wesley church, Shippen Street, Philadelphia. It is called the Delaware Conference, under the control of the Methodist Episcopal Church. Includes Weaver's complaint against Isaac Bredden, who took A.M.E. ordination vows at the last Philadelphia Annual Conference (Salem, N.J.), was sent to the Oxford Circuit, stayed about a month, and left for the M.E. Church.
people: A.M.E. itinerant preacher, Oxford Circuit; left for the M.E. Delaware Conference

articles.headline: Justice and Honor to the Brave (editorial on the Crater)
articles.summary: In the late and terrible assault made upon the enemy's works in front of Petersburg, some of the unprincipled Copperhead papers have been trying their utmost to make it appear that the sole cause of the failure of Grant's brilliant onslaught was owing to the colored troops quailing and giving way beneath the withering fire of the enemy's guns. Defends the Black troops at the Crater (July 30, 1864) and demands that the Government protect captured colored soldiers.

articles.headline: Letter from Cape Island
articles.author: J. H. Turpin
articles.summary: Cape Island, August 1st. Rev. Weaver: Sir: Permit me through your most valuable, so interesting, and honorable organ, the Christian Recorder... Describes sea bathing at Cape Island; a visit to the Bethel church 'which our bishops and fathers planted here on the seashore'; Rev. Stephen Smith preached in the morning, the writer in the afternoon and Rev. Teagle at night; meets Bro. Abraham Fields in his grocery store, Mrs. Schaff and Mrs. Tengle; invites Weaver to the Harvest Home celebration next Wednesday week.

articles.headline: Our Army Correspondence (43d U.S.C.T.)
articles.author: J. C. Brock
articles.summary: Camp near Petersburg, Va. Dear Recorder: Having a few leisure moments, I again devote myself to writing, to let our readers know how we are coming on. Reports Sergeant George Mabotey [VERIFY] of Baltimore, Co. G, 39th Regiment, killed in the trenches; Corporal Brewster, of Philadelphia, Co. C, 43d Regiment, badly wounded in hand and head; a visit to the division hospital with Rev. Mr. Underdue, of Philadelphia, now chaplain of the 39th Regt.; asks Northern ladies to form benevolent associations. Signed J. C. Brock, Commissary Sergeant, 43d Regt. U. S. C. T.

articles.headline: The Ladies' Union Association (letter)
articles.author: Observer
articles.summary: The Ladies' Union Association deserve the credit and support of the community, as it is laboring successfully for the colored soldiers who have gone from our midst. Last Tuesday we found them with two machines, at work... Pearl St. Church sent them quite a donation. We understand that they will shortly make their first Annual Report. Philadelphia, July 28th, 1864.

articles.headline: Letter from Woodbury (on Isaiah Breddon)

articles.summary: Woodbury, July 29th, 1864. Mr. Editor: Rev. and Dear Brother: I take this opportunity of writing these few lines to inform you that it has come to my knowledge recently, that since our last Annual Conference sat in Salem, N. Church, on last Thursday, the 21st inst. Signed Richard Barney, Minister.

articles.headline: Letter on patronizing colored business men (conclusion; Macedonia church debt)
articles.author: West Jersey
articles.summary: Continued from page 2 (not in our copy): ...want is, fewer of those happy gatherings, where men delight to dispose of some rare orations, and more of the practical. articles.headline: Letter from A. W. Wayman (episcopal tour)
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: It may be interesting to the readers of your paper, and the members of the Church, to hear from those who were recently elected to assist in the superintendency of the Church. At the meeting of the bishops of the A. M. E. Church, just before the close of the late General Conference, we were assigned to the 2d Episcopal District, consisting of the Philadelphia and New York Conferences. Itinerary: New Brunswick (Rev. Wm. A. Offer); dedication of a new church at Mount Holly, N.J., June 26, under Rev. Theodore Gould; Burlington; Bordentown (Rev. James Holland's charge [VERIFY]); Port Deposit, Md. (Rev. Stephen P. Stevenson, removed to Oxford, Pa.). 'Sunday, 30th, was spent in Philadelphia. Rev. Wm. Moore, at Bethel, Rev. A. L. Stanford, at Union, and Rev. Jos. H. Smith, at Wesley, are all men of the right stamp.' Cape May (Brother Jay), Camden and Wilmington. Baltimore, Aug. 9th, 1864.

articles.headline: To the Colored People of the United States
articles.author: Sarah [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Having presumed to take up my pen to write a few lines for your valuable paper, I hope that they will meet with your approbation. articles.headline: Is Rev. Morgan Dead? / Another Mass Meeting / Our New Disciplines (editorial notes)
articles.summary: Is Rev. Morgan dead? This question is being asked us daily and hourly. The only answer we can give is that we cannot say for certain. Our correspondent, who furnished us the list of casualties for our [last] edition, will probably enlighten us on that point in his next letter. Another Mass Meeting: We understand that there was another Mass Meeting of our colored citizens held in the Sansom Hall on last Thursday evening; but, unfortunately, as our reporter was not present at the meeting, we are therefore unable to furnish our readers with any material account of its proceedings. Our New Disciplines: a few now ready; cloth 50 [VERIFY], sheep 45, extra 60 cents.

articles.headline: The Trustees of the A.M.E. Church and Chas. Smith (West Chester court case)
articles.author: G. W. Peterson [VERIFY]
articles.summary: West Chester, August 8, 1864. Mr. Editor: The Court in which the Trustees of the A. M. E. Church had a suit pending held its session, and decided in our favor. The circumstance was as follows: Charles Smith, once a member of the A. M. E. Church, was expelled, Nov. 4th, 1858; since which time he has been disturbing our Class Meetings. Last May, George Dennis and myself put him out from said Class, and in so doing, he fell down stairs; upon this he entered suit against us for assault and battery... it has now been decided by the Judge that Class-leaders and Trustees have full power to remove any person from the room who has no right there.

articles.headline: Do Colored Men Make Good Soldiers?
articles.author: Sarah
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Allow me once more to encroach upon your valuable space, for the purpose of refuting a charge too often made, namely, that colored men do not make good soldiers. articles.headline: An Obituary (Green Singleton, Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: On the life, character, and death of Green [printed 'Greeen' or 'Grecen'] Singleton, who was born in Kentucky, near Lexington. He was born a slave in 1818; was married in the year 1841; embraced religion in the year 1845, and joined the Methodist Church in Kentucky, and in the year 1847 was sold into Mississippi. In 1848 he purchased his freedom by his industry and economy, and the hard, fatiguing labour of his dear wife. In the same year (1848) he came to Philadelphia with his certificate, and with it joined the A. M. E. Union Church, on Coates Street, where he continued a worthy and acceptable member while he lived. (Also named, reading uncertain: Green Singleton [VERIFY] (deceased May 10, 1864, aged 46; member, Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street).)

articles.summary: Camp left of Petersburg, Va., August 28th, 1864. Dear Recorder: There is nothing of importance that has occurred among us since my last letter. events.name: Convention of A. M. E. and A. M. E. Zion delegates on church union, Wesley Church
events.location: Wesley Church, Lombard St., Philadelphia
events.description: Delegates appointed by the General Conference of the A. M. E. Church and the General Conference of the A. M. E. Zion Church held a convention in Wesley Church, Lombard St., Phila., on the 14th, 15th and 16th of June 1864 'for the purpose of effecting a basis of union with the two bodies' (circular: 'assembled in Convention in Philadelphia, June 14th, 1864, remaining in session three days'). It adopted ten 'Articles of Confederation': the united body to be 'The United African Methodist Episcopal Church in America'; agreement in doctrine, worship, itinerancy and Methodism; the episcopacy kept, with Zion's choice of superintendents left to its General Conference; lay delegation; a two-thirds congregational vote to reject a minister; Disciplines to go to a committee of twelve; ratification by members, quarterly and annual conferences and a United General Conference of 1868, the two connections remaining distinct until then. The convention appointed a committee of Revs. S. Jones, H. Davis, J. Trusty, J. Woodlye and A. L. Stanford to publish 25,000 copies of the basis. The Recorder's Philadelphia correspondent complains that an unnamed 'Mr. Busybody' printed and sold the circular for his own profit.

events.name: Chester (Pa.) circuit first quarterly meeting
events.location: Chester, Pa.
events.description: Editorial report (Elisha Weaver's 'we'): the first quarterly meeting for the circuit was held 'last Saturday and Sunday' (July 9 and 10, 1864). Weaver left Philadelphia on Saturday on the Wilmington boat at half-past two with brother John Cornish, the minister on the circuit, and stayed with 'our much-esteemed and beloved brother Murphy and his kind lady, in Free Street'; brother Murphy is a deacon of long standing. Quarterly conference Saturday night (many members delayed by harvest). Sabbath: love feast 9 to half-past ten; at eleven a Baptist preacher spoke, two exhortations, and the preacher in charge closed. At half-past one, the funeral of the child of brother Turner, who was drowned a few days prior; brother Turner used to be stationed in Wilmington, Del. Afternoon: Weaver's sacramental discourse and the Lord's Supper, assisted by brother Cornish and brother Murphy. At night brother Frisby Cooper, a local preacher of Wilmington, Del., preached, followed by brother Lloyd, another local preacher, from Philadelphia. Only two subscribers taken for the Recorder. The minister announced that sister Murray, a lady preacher, would hold a bush meeting on brother Cornish's circuit; Weaver objects to anyone, man or woman, officiating in public without being legally authorized.

events.name: Mass meeting on exclusion from the city passenger railways, Sansom Street Hall
events.location: Sansom Street Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: 'The Enthusiastic Gathering of Colored Persons in Sansom St. Hall.' The call for a mass-meeting of colored persons to take action in reference to their exclusion from the city passenger railways met on 'last Tuesday evening' (July 26, 1864). Prayer by Rev. A. L. Stanford. Officers: President, J. C. Bowers; Vice-Presidents, James Needham, Rev'ds. Elisha Weaver, A. L. Stanford, J. B. Reeve, J. P. Trusty, S. Smith, Messrs. T. J. Bowers, J. C. Bustill, G. W. Goines [as read], W. H. Riley, F. Turner; Secretaries, J. C. White, Jr., Chas. Colly [as read], J. W. Simpson, and John Wolf, of Harrisburg. Bowers said colored persons rode the cars in Boston, New York, New Orleans and Pittsburgh, while Philadelphia compelled them to walk or stand on the front platform; he cited the cases of Rev. Mr. Alston, the matron of the West Philadelphia Orphans' Home (name left blank) and Capt. Robert Small[s], and mothers of soldiers at Camp Wm. Penn forced onto the platform, and the company that went to Harrisburg in 1863. Committees: on the car question, Rev. J. C. Gibbs, J. C. White, Jr., J. C. Bustill; on the state of the country, D. D. Turner, St. Geo. R. Taylor, Jas. McCrummill. Resolutions (read by Rev. J. C. Gibbs) to agitate by all lawful means; recommending 'the League formed by the colored people of this city' to raise a fund for agitation through the press; appealing to the Christian churches; denouncing the sight of respectable women standing on platforms with sons, husbands and brothers in U.S. uniform; thanking the Union League of New York for providing counsel; and noting the companies ignore 25,000 colored inhabitants. Speeches by Rev. Jonathan Gibbs, Mr. A. Green (on the state-of-the-country resolutions), Prof. A. M. Green, and Robt. Hamilton, editor of the Anglo-African (New York). Closed with the 'John Brown song' and 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

events.name: Delaware Conference (first colored annual conference of the M.E. Church) organized
events.location: John Wesley church, Shippen Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Local preachers of the Methodist Episcopal Church organized into the Delaware Conference by Bishop Janes, assisted by Bishop Simpson, Dr. Durbin and others (white M.E. officials), some eighteen or twenty members, most grey-headed. A presiding elder recommended a 'brother Jackson' for elder's orders; members objected that he held too much with the 'Allenites' (A.M.E.); Dr. Durbin settled the matter and Jackson was elected. Saturday July 30 session; Bishop Simpson spoke, referring to the Institute (High School) for Colored Youth; Bishop Janes presented Kidder's Homiletics to each member; next session voted for Wilmington, Del. Ordinations on Sunday: deacons at John Wesley by Bishop Janes, elders at Zoar church. Weaver adds that Isaac Bredden, ordained by the A.M.E. Philadelphia Conference at Salem, N.J., and sent to the Oxford Circuit, left for this conference.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- first box to wounded colored soldiers at Norfolk
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Association sending boxes to wounded colored soldiers at Norfolk; cash from a committee of the Baptist Church, Pearl St. ($6.50), Mr. G. G. Iredell, Mr. J. Simpson, Mr. L. Seymour ($1.00 each), A Friend (25 cts), total $9.75; goods from Mr. H. Gordon, Miss Thompson, Mrs. Matilda Bates [VERIFY], Mrs. Julia Williams, Mrs. Robinson, Mrs. Caesar, Mrs. Rigby, a Friend and Miss Jones, a little girl, and the Association itself (wine, jelly, corn starch, farina, tomatoes, fans, 13 shirts, 32 towels, handkerchiefs, pickles, 7 double wrappers). Articles may be left at the houses of the officers: President V. E. Dorsey [VERIFY], 615 [VERIFY] Clifton St.; Treasurer A. E. Mills, 1015 Lombard St.; Secretary R. Louisa Iredell [VERIFY], 917 Washington Street. A letter signed Observer (July 28) reports two sewing machines at work and an annual report forthcoming.

events.name: Camp meeting near Cold Spring, Cape Island (A.M.E.)
events.location: woods one mile east of Cold Spring, three miles west of Cape Island, N.J.
events.description: Camp meeting commencing Thursday Aug. 25 to pay the debt of the A.M.E. Church at Cold Spring; boat arrangements from Philadelphia. J. P. Jay, minister in charge; Joshua Woodlin, elder.

events.name: Harvest Home, Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church, Princeton
events.location: woods of Mrs. Potter, near the railroad depot, Princeton, N.J.
events.description: Grand harvest home for the new Mount Pisgah church; dinner and refreshments in the woods, several eminent speakers; evening exhibition by the Sabbath School in the church, doors open 7 o'clock, admittance 15 cents. Rev. Henry Davis, Elder; Mr. James Schenck [VERIFY], Superintendent.

events.name: Mass meeting of colored citizens at Sansom Hall
events.location: Sansom Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: 'Another Mass Meeting of our colored citizens held in the Sansom Hall on last Thursday evening' (Aug. 18, 1864, counting back from the Aug. 20 issue; possibly Aug. 11 if the item was set a week earlier). The Recorder's reporter was not present; no proceedings printed. Context: the run-up to the Syracuse National Convention of Colored Men (October 1864).

events.name: Harvest Home and Sabbath-school concert, A.M.E. Church, Burlington
events.location: Burlington, N.J.
events.description: Sabbath school excursion and evening concert of vocal and instrumental music under Professor A. Burris of Philadelphia; dinner in the grove; proceeds for the church. Rev. T. Gould, pastor.

events.name: Union Camp Meeting at Carpenter's Landing, Gloucester County, N.J.
events.location: woods at Fort Jessup [VERIFY], Carpenter's Landing, Gloucester Co., N.J.
events.description: Union camp meeting under Rev. J. B. Trusty, A. L. Stanford and other speakers; tent arrangements through J. B. Trusty at Wesley church, Lombard St.; boat from Walnut Street Wharf, Woodbury cars, fare 35 cents. Start date read 'August 23d' [VERIFY].

events.name: West Chester A.M.E. trustees win assault suit brought by Charles Smith
events.location: West Chester, Pa.
events.description: Court session (before Aug. 8, 1864) decided in favor of the A.M.E. trustees. Charles Smith, expelled Nov. 4, 1858, kept disturbing class meetings; in May 1864 George Dennis and the writer (G. W. Peterson [VERIFY]) put him out of the class, he fell down stairs, and sued for assault and battery. The judge held class-leaders and trustees may remove anyone with no right in the room. The writer notes the 'Recording Steward' had argued the contrary.

events.name: Mass meeting of colored citizens on the Passenger Railway (streetcar) exclusion
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street, Philadelphia
events.description: Public meeting pursuant to call. Chairman John C. Bowers, president of the Union League; vice presidents J. Colburn [VERIFY], Ebenezer Black, James W. Brown, George W. Gaines [VERIFY] (also printed Gotnes, Golnes) and Robert Adger; secretaries St. George R. Taylor and Davis D. Turner. Minutes of the previous meeting at Sansom St. Hall read and approved and its sentiments reaffirmed. Prof. A. M. Green, secretary of the Union League, read a letter previously approved by the League, addressed to the presidents, superintendents and others managing the Passenger Railway companies of Philadelphia; unanimously adopted (the editor says the letter came too late to print). George W. Gaines [VERIFY] spoke on the cars; Rev. Mr. Cary of New York spoke; Rev. J. [B.] Trusty appealed for contributions to prosecute the claims of the colored citizens to the use of the Passenger Railway cars; $34.16 [VERIFY] raised for the hall. Prof. Green, for the committee of arrangement, reported $26.00 [VERIFY] spent at the Sansom Street Hall meeting (advertising $6.00 [VERIFY], hall rent $15.00, publishing resolutions in the Press $12.00, publishing minutes $7.00) and spoke for soldiers' families, the wounded at Point Lookout, and the call for a National Convention. Green's announcement that 'one Rev. J. H. Smith' was denouncing public meetings for rights led to a brief debate with Rev. William Moore, settled amicably. Church representatives pledged their churches to the fight against 'the outrages of the Passenger Railway companies', prominent among them Rev. William H. Moore of Bethel, Geo. W. Gaines [VERIFY], Mr. John Boling [VERIFY] and John C. Bowers. St. George R. Taylor proposed a system for collecting funds for prosecuting the railway cars; the chair referred it to the League.
attendees: chairman; president of the Union League

events.name: West Chester festival for the Recorder for colored soldiers
events.location: Colored School-house, West Chester, Pa.
events.description: Festival in the Colored School-house raised a fund to send the Christian Recorder to colored soldiers; $13 delivered to Weaver (the Monday before Aug. 27). Managers: Mrs. Mary [VERIFY] A. Rather [VERIFY], Mrs. Annie Hicks [VERIFY], J. Simons [VERIFY], Wm. Jones, Wm. Boyer, Ed. A. Cheriche [VERIFY].

events.name: Bush meeting, Centre Valley, Reading Circuit
events.location: Centre [VERIFY] Valley, Reading Circuit, Chester Co., Pa.
events.description: Bush meeting commencing Saturday Aug. 27. Minister in charge Rev. W. H. Norris [VERIFY]; presiding elder Rev. J. H. Henson [VERIFY] (names blurred).

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- relief for sick and wounded colored soldiers at Summit House Hospital
events.location: Summit House Hospital, Darby Road, West Philadelphia
events.description: Report signed J. H. Wilson, dated August 29th [VERIFY day], 1864. Between four and five hundred sick and wounded colored soldiers, maimed before Petersburg, at the Summit House Hospital. On Tuesday and Friday of the previous week a gentleman collected about $25 and, with Miss Amelia Mills of the Ladies' Union Association, purchased 100 watermelons, 4 baskets of peaches, 4 baskets of citrons, 1 basket of apples, sundry pies, cakes and 6 pounds of tobacco, distributed at the hospital by Miss Mills, Miss Cole, Miss Iredell and Mrs. Jackson. Donations as printed: Dr. Parlow [VERIFY] 2.00; Dr. Parlow, Jr. [VERIFY] 1.00; J. G. Bowers [VERIFY] .50; P. Buchanan .50; Mrs. Hall .50; Morris Brown .25; Mr. Adger .50; R. Adger .25; Dr. Wilson 2.00; Jas. Brown 1.00; L. Douglass .50; Thos. Bowers .50; Rev. J. P. B. Eddy 1.00; Cash .25; Dr. Longfellow .50; Wm. Kemble [VERIFY] .50; Mr. Brister [VERIFY] 1.00; E. S. Venning .75; Lazarus [VERIFY] Brown .50 or .60; Mrs. Whitington [VERIFY] 1.00; Mrs. Vandyke .25; Wm. Cooper .25; A. Cassey .50; J. C. Bustill 2.00; Mr. Johnson 1.00; St. George R. Taylor 5.00; Gilpin Peer [VERIFY] 1.00; Mr. Anthony 1.00; Ladies' Union 5.00. Total $31.00. Expenditures Aug 23 and Aug 26 (tobacco, citrons, apples, peaches, watermelons, porterage, hauling, carriage, tolls, cash to soldiers), total $29.34 [VERIFY]; balance in hand $1.66. The watermelons, citrons and peaches distributed on the 26th were the donation of Dr. P. H. Lowber [VERIFY]. Donations may be left with Miss Mills, 1015 Lombard St.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Sabbath-school excursion to Diamond Cottage
events.location: Diamond Cottage grove (Philadelphia)
events.description: Annual Sabbath-school excursion of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, reported by J. H. Turpin, Philadelphia, August 31st, 1864. About 3 o'clock the trumpet called the children to feasting and addresses. The writer spoke at the invitation of Revs. Smith and Moore and the Superintendent, Mr. Louis Seymour; then Rev. Stephen Smith, Wm. Moore, Father Henry and T. G. Steward addressed a crowd estimated at three thousand. The repast was provided by the superintendent and teachers. Present in the grove: Revs. Edward Hammonds [printed 'Hammonde'], P. C. Davis and Edward M. Peck, young theological students of the Ashmun Seminary.

events.name: Installation of Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller, Pearl Street Baptist Church
events.location: Pearl Street Baptist Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller, late of Albany, N. Y., to be installed as pastor of the Pearl street Baptist Church of this city on Thursday evening, Sept. 8th, at a quarter before 8 o'clock.

events.name: West Philadelphia Circuit -- second course of Quarterly Meetings
events.location: Norristown, Germantown and West Philadelphia
events.description: General Class at Norristown Friday evening Sept. 16; Quarterly Conference Saturday Sept. 17, 2 P. M.; Germantown Sept. 24-25; West Philadelphia Oct. 1-2. Notice signed Peter Gardener, Preacher in charge of W. Phila. Circuit.
attendees: preacher in charge, West Philadelphia Circuit

events.name: Bishop Wayman's visitation, Philadelphia stops
events.location: Germantown; West Philadelphia; Zion Mission, Philadelphia
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's September appointments (Baltimore, Aug 26, 1864): Sept 11 Wrightsville, Columbia, Lancaster; Sept 12 Marietta; 13 Conestoga; 14 Pottsville; 15 Reading; 16 Deep Valley; Sabbath Sept 18, 10 o'clock Germantown, 3 o'clock West Philadelphia, at night Zion Mission, Philadelphia; Sept 25 Gouldtown, Bridgeton, Springfield N. J.; 27 Salem; 28 Rushtown; 29 Woodbury; 30 Snow Hill, N. J.

events.name: Bush meeting near Millville, N. J., for new church
events.location: woods near Millville, N. J.
events.description: Bush meeting commencing September 3d, 1864, for the benefit of the new church to be erected at Millville; trains from Walnut Street wharf at 6, 10 and 4.30. Notice signed Joshua Woodlin.

events.name: Frankford colored citizens' meeting -- delegate elected to the National Convention
events.location: A. M. E. Bethel church, Oxford [VERIFY] street, Frankford
events.description: Public meeting of the colored citizens of Frankford, Monday evening, August 22d, 1864. Chairman Mr. Randal [VERIFY] Pleasants, Sr.; Secretary Mr. Joseph G. Fry. On motion of Mr. William S. Walker, seconded by Mr. William Watson, the call for a national convention of colored citizens of the United States was read; resolved to elect one delegate, furnished with credentials, to represent Frankford in the coming National Convention 'that is to be held in the city of New York on the Fourth Day of October, 1864' (as printed; the convention met at Syracuse). Nominating committee: Mr. Peter R. Brake [VERIFY], Mr. Jacob [VERIFY] Myers, Mr. William Watson, Mr. Job Trusty and Rev. Henderson Davis. The committee nominated Mr. Henderson Davis, Jr., and Mr. Morris; Mr. Samuel Morris was elected delegate. Resolutions offered by Mr. Lewis Bedford [VERIFY] (continued on p3): the delegate to receive no emolument beyond expenses; the citizens to raise $35 for his expenses; a treasurer to be elected by ballot; weekly Monday meetings until the sum is raised; full approbation of the election of Samuel Morris, 'a gentleman and a scholar, and the right man in the right place'. All adopted unanimously. (Also named, reading uncertain: Randal Pleasants, Sr. [VERIFY] (chairman); Jacob Myers [VERIFY] (nominating committee).)
attendees: elected delegate to the National Convention

events.name: Camden circuit A.M.E. Sabbath-school procession to Diamond Cottage
events.location: Camden, East Camden and Kaighnsville, N. J., to Diamond Cottage
events.description: The A.M.E. Sabbath Schools of Camden, East Camden and Kaighnsville to assemble at 9 o'clock and march in procession of scholars, teachers, parents and friends to Diamond Cottage to sing. Signed T. G. Steward, Minister in Charge; H. Mackey, George [VERIFY] White, B. F. Brown, Superintendents.

events.name: Union Baptist Church (Minster St.) ladies' Grand Festival
events.location: basement of Union Baptist Church, Minster Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Grand Festival Entertainment by the ladies of Union Baptist church, Wednesday and Thursday evenings, Sept. 28 and 29; admission 25 cts., single evening 15 cts.; tickets at the Christian Recorder office.

events.name: Bordentown A.M.E. ladies' surprise visit to the pastor
events.location: pastor's house, Bordentown, N. J.
events.description: Procession headed by Mrs. Unice Collins presented the minister with $13.30 in money and valuables to make $20. Committee: Mrs. Unice Collins, Miss Sarah Chesman [VERIFY], Mrs. Mary Sullivan, Miss Margaret Davis. Letter signed James Hollon [VERIFY].

events.name: Flag presentation to the 45th and 127th U.S.C.T. at Camp William Penn
events.location: Camp William Penn
events.description: About 2:15 P.M. the 45th and 127th USCT and part of the 141st [as printed] formed in line and paraded for visitors. The reporter visited the Sutler's Department under 'our well known and esteemed citizen, Mr. William Still'. At four o'clock General Birney, for the Supervisory Committee for recruiting colored troops, presented an ensign to the 45th, received by Major Bahe [VERIFY]; the lawyer Charles Gibbons presented a flag to the 127th ('The Government that acknowledges black men as soldiers, at the same time recognizes black men as her citizens'), received by Lieutenant-Colonel Given. Cheers for the Union, the Supervisory Committee and the Stars and Stripes; the Regimental Band played. (White officers and committee members named in text only.)

events.name: Independent Grand Tabernacles of Love and Charity of Pennsylvania -- quarterly convocation and annual election
events.location: their hall, South Eleventh below Pine Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Called to order by the Grand Worthy Superior, Bro. Jas. H. Smith; prayer by Grand Chaplain Bro. James Hamilton; minutes of June 3d, 1864 approved. Reports approved from Jerusalem Tabernacle No. 1; Prudence No. 4; King Solomon No. 6; Celestial No. 7; Olive Branch No. 8; Smith's No. 9; King David No. 10; Athenaeum No. 13 [VERIFY number]; State Tab.; Henry Brooks Tab., Westchester; St. James Tab., Norristown; Isaac Emory Tab., of Boston; James T. Robinson Tab., Thornbury. Letter from Dr. John S. Rock of Boston, Grand District Deputy Superior for New England and Past W. S. of Isaac Emory Tabernacle. Bro. Henry Brooks reported on his year visiting the State Tabernacles (prosperous though many male members had gone to war). Elected and installed by Bro. James H. Smith: Grand Worthy Superior, Rev. Bro. James Hamilton; Grand Worthy Vice, Sister Jane Farris; Grand Deputy Superior, Bro. Henry Brooks; Grand Worthy Treasurer, Bro. James T. Robinson; Grand Worthy Chaplain, Rev. Bro. Stephen Smith; Grand Worthy Scribe, Bro. Nath. Wiggins; Grand Assistant Scribe, Sister Sarah Allen; Grand Conductress, Sister Hannah Cisco [VERIFY]; Grand Inner Sentinel, Bro. Thos. Shupherd; Grand Outer Sentinel, Bro. Edw. Johnson. District Deputies: Bro. John Brown, Pennsylvania District; Rev. Bro. Whiting, Allegheny, Pittsburg and west of the mountains; Bro. John S. Rock, New England; Bro. Moses Dickson, St. Louis. Collation for the State delegates. Attest: Nathaniel Wiggins, Grand Scribe.

events.name: Daughters of Zion festival, Mount Zion Church, Trenton
events.location: basement of Mount Zion Church, Trenton, N. J.
events.description: Festival by the Daughters of Zion, a society of some years' standing whose object is to help pay the minister's board; addresses; admission 10 cents. Notice signed Thomas H. Cooper, Minister in Charge.

events.name: Burlington Circuit Sabbath-school celebrations (Evesham and Burlington)
events.location: groves at Evesham (Aug 23) and Burlington (Sept 1), N. J.
events.description: Per Rev. T. Gould: Evesham Sabbath-school celebration Aug 23 cleared seventy dollars for a new church; Burlington Sabbath-school anniversary and Harvest Home Sept 1 with addresses by Rev. J. H. Turpin, Brothers C. H. Hedges, J. S. Thompson and Rev. William Offer; Rev. J. H. Smith closed with anecdotes. Evening concert in the church under Mr. A. Burris [VERIFY first initial]. Committee of Arrangements cleared one hundred and one [VERIFY] dollars toward the church debt.

events.name: Philadelphia Conference collections for Bishop Campbell's outfit to California
events.location: Philadelphia Conference circuits and stations; Philadelphia
events.description: Acknowledgment signed J. P. Campbell, Philadelphia, Sept. 16, 1864. Burlington Circuit, Rev. T. Gould, $18.87. Trenton Circuit, Rev. T. H. Cooper: Trenton $8.97, Pennington $10.25, Mrs. Rachel McConnell [VERIFY] $1.00. Princeton Circuit, Rev. H. Davis, $7.30. Bridge St. Station, Rev. J. M. Williams: collection in church $16.70, Mr. Ross $5.00, Mrs. Jones $1.00, A Friend $1.00. Brunswick Station, Rev. Wm. Offer, $3.00. Bordentown Circuit, Rev. J. Hollan: Bordentown $7.00, Allentown $1.32, Rev. A. C. Crippen $1.00, Miss Alice Raynor [VERIFY] $1.00. Salem Circuit, Rev. J. Long [VERIFY], $11.18; Mrs. Anna George $1.00. Bridgeton Circuit, Rev. J. Woodlyn, $3.50. Union Church Station, Rev. A. L. Standford, $12.75. Bethel Church Station, Rev. Wm. Moore: church collection $26.53; Mrs. M. Butler, Mrs. E. White, Mrs. A. Laws, Mrs. J. Custis [VERIFY], Miss Mary Still, Mr. P. D. Lewis, Mr. J. Masten [VERIFY], Mr. J. Berry, $1.00 each; Mrs. P. Harris, Mrs. A. Downs, Miss S. Miles, .50 each. Wesley Church Station, Rev. J. H. Smith, $31.65; Mrs. E. Clarke .50. Zion Mission, Rev. W. H. Winder, $5.00. Philadelphia A.M.E. Preachers' Meeting, $5.00. Allen Chapel, Cincinnati, Rev. J. A. Shorter, $23.35. Further gifts to No. 832 [VERIFY] Carpenter Street.

events.name: Funeral of Thomas Todd, Bethel class-leader
events.location: from his residence, Mebo [VERIFY] Street above Race, to Olive Cemetery
events.description: Thomas Todd, one of the oldest members of Bethel, died Friday Sept 16, 1864, aged about ninety, at his residence on Mebo [VERIFY] Street above Race. Born in Delaware, formerly enslaved by Nathan McGill; joined the Union Church there, then the A.M.E. Church; settled in Philadelphia and was a member forty years and a class-leader at Bethel upwards of thirty years. Left a wife and several sons. Remains deposited in the Olive Cemetery on Tuesday, Sept 20, with many citizens present.

events.name: Lombard Street (Central) Presbyterian Sabbath-school concert
events.location: Presbyterian Church, Lombard St., Philadelphia
events.description: Grand concert by the Sabbath School of the Lombard St. Presbyterian Church (Rev. Mr. Reeves, pastor) on 'last Wednesday evening', conducted by their teacher Professor A. Burris; church crowded; refreshments by the ladies in the basement.

events.name: Bishop Campbell visits the Union A.M.E. Sabbath-school
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church Sabbath-school, Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday afternoon visit by Bishop Campbell with ex-superintendent I. C. Wears; Campbell recalled being a scholar in the first Sabbath-school established at Bethel Church, Sixth Street above Lombard. A white M. E. Sabbath-school man named Tyler also spoke. Bishop en route to California. Letter signed A. B., Philadelphia, Sept 19, 1864.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- soldiers' relief at Summit House and Satterlee Hospitals
events.location: Summit House and Satterlee Hospitals, West Philadelphia
events.description: Letter signed 'Friend', Sept 21, 1864: the Ladies' Union Association (Miss A. Mills, President) has distributed fruits, dainties and tobacco twice a week; about 800 melons, 25 baskets of peaches, 25 of citrons, apples, pies, jellies and 50 lbs of tobacco with clay pipes, through the Association, the Statistical Society, the Seventh St. Presbyterian Church, Bethel, and individuals: Dr. C. H. Lowber [VERIFY], J. C. White, Dr. Wilson, Mrs. Tingle, Mrs. Sebastian and Mrs. Stokely. The Sabbath school of the Seventh Street Church gave up its annual festival and gave the whole sum (nearly fifty dollars). Donations: R. R. Turner [VERIFY] $3.00; Thos. R. Jordan [VERIFY] $5.00; cash .50; about 25 lbs of tobacco through Chas. Gordon. Bethel planned a visit that week; the ladies went out that day with fifty pies, the gift of Mrs. Cliff.

events.name: A.M.E. / A.M.E. Zion union circulars issued
events.location: Book Store, No. 619 Pine St.; 931 Leithgow St., Philadelphia
events.description: The Philadelphia correspondent (unsigned) says the July convention of fifty delegates (equal numbers from each Church) adopted a union platform; circulars containing the platform or articles of agreement are printed by the committee: Revs. J. H. Trusty, H. Davis, S. T. Jones and A. L. Stanford. Circulars previously put out by Rev. William H. Jones 'were not genuine' (no authority from the Convention). Genuine circulars at the Book Store, 619 Pine St. (5 cents), or from A. L. Stanford, District Book Steward, at his residence No. 931 Leithgow Street ($4 per hundred). Also p2 col 3 notice (Sep 17): Articles of Consolidation for sale at the Recorder office.

events.name: Corner-stone laying, Green's Tabernacle No. 6 hall, Woodbury, N. J.
events.location: Woodbury, N. J.
events.description: Corner-stone of a hall for Green's Tabernacle No. 6, I. O. of B. S. of L. and C. (Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity), Thursday Sept 29 at 2 P.M.; officers of the I. G. Tabernacle for Pennsylvania invited; dinner for the benefit of the Tabernacle in the grove if fine.
